init.scope: systemd itself: the first program Linux starts. It starts and watches every other service.
systemd-journald: Keeps the system log (what happened and when). Stays on this computer, capped at 200 MB.
systemd-journal-flush: Moves early-boot log messages onto the disk.
systemd-udevd: Notices hardware as it appears (USB sticks, keyboards, screens) and loads the right drivers.
systemd-logind: Tracks who is logged in, handles the power button, lid and sleep.
systemd-timesyncd: Keeps your clock correct by asking a public time server. Needed for secure websites; sends no personal data.
systemd-tmpfiles-clean: Deletes old temporary files once a day.
systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer: Once a day: removes old temporary files.
systemd-random-seed: Saves randomness between boots so encryption keys are strong from the start.
systemd-update-utmp: Records boots and shutdowns in the login history.
systemd-user-sessions: Allows logins once the system is ready.
systemd-remount-fs: Mounts your disks with the right options at startup.
systemd-modules-load: Loads extra drivers listed in the configuration.
systemd-exit: Helps your session shut down cleanly.
dbus: The message bus: lets programs talk to each other on this computer (never over the network).
dbus-broker: The message bus: lets programs talk to each other on this computer (never over the network).
NetworkManager: Connects to Wi-Fi and wired networks. Its 'phone home' connectivity check is turned off in GlassOS.
NetworkManager-dispatcher: Runs small scripts when a network connects or disconnects.
NetworkManager-wait-online: Waits for the network during startup.
wpa_supplicant: Handles Wi-Fi security (logging in to WPA2/WPA3 networks).
polkit: Decides which programs may do admin-level things like shutting down or mounting a drive.
rtkit-daemon: Gives audio priority so sound doesn't crackle, without running audio as admin.
udisks2: Mounts USB drives and disks when you click them in Files.
greetd: The login manager: starts your desktop after you log in.
getty@: A text login prompt on a virtual console (Ctrl+Alt+F1–F6).
serial-getty@: A text login prompt on a serial port (used by virtual machines).
nftables: The firewall: blocks unsolicited incoming connections.
alsa-restore: Restores your sound card volume from last time.
alsa-state: Saves and restores sound card settings.
glassos-boot-sound: Plays the boot sound from your sound pack before the login screen.
plymouth-quit: Hides the boot animation once the desktop is ready.
plymouth-quit-wait: Waits for the boot animation to finish.
plymouth-read-write: Lets the boot animation save its timing data.
keyboard-setup: Applies your keyboard layout at startup.
console-setup: Sets the font and layout of text consoles.
live-config: Sets up the live USB session (only when running from USB/DVD).
lima-guestagent: Only present in the build machine: shares files with the host (not part of GlassOS).
user@: Your personal service manager: starts and watches your own background services and apps.
user-runtime-dir@: Creates your private temporary folder when you log in.
e2scrub_all: Checks ext4 disks for hidden errors.
e2scrub_all.timer: Once a week: checks ext4 disks for hidden errors (only with LVM snapshots; usually does nothing).
fstrim: Tells SSDs which space is free, keeping them fast.
fstrim.timer: Once a week: tells your SSD which space is free so it stays fast.
dpkg-db-backup: Backs up the list of installed packages.
dpkg-db-backup.timer: Once a day: backs up the list of installed packages (on this computer only).
apt-daily.timer: Turned off in GlassOS: would check for updates in the background.
apt-daily-upgrade.timer: Turned off in GlassOS: would install updates in the background.
pipewire: The sound server: mixes audio from every app and sends it to your speakers or headphones.
pipewire-pulse: Lets apps built for PulseAudio play sound through PipeWire.
wireplumber: Picks your speakers, headphones and microphone and remembers their volume.
filter-chain: Optional PipeWire audio effects (not used unless you set them up).
glass-soundd: GlassOS sound daemon: plays your sound pack for USB, charger, battery, network and error events.
gvfs-daemon: Lets Files show the trash, USB drives and network shares.
gvfs-metadata: Remembers small details about files (like custom icons) for Files.
gvfs-udisks2-volume-monitor: Tells Files when a USB drive or disk is plugged in.
xfconfd: Stores settings for Files and Text Editor.
thunar: Files running in the background so windows open instantly.
at-spi-dbus-bus: Accessibility: lets screen readers talk to apps.
gpg-agent: Holds encryption keys while you use them (only runs if something needs it).
dirmngr: Fetches encryption key information (only runs if something needs it).
keyboxd: Stores encryption keys (only runs if something needs it).
glass-dock: The GlassOS dock at the bottom of the screen.
glass-topbar: The top bar: menu, window title, clock, battery, Wi-Fi and volume.
glass-notifications: Shows notification bubbles in the top-right corner.
glass-idle: Dims and locks the screen when you're away.
glass-polkit: Asks for your password when an app needs admin rights (and tells you which app).
bluetooth: Bluetooth: connects headphones, mice and keyboards. Off until you turn it on.
